second_defensible.reason: With no value labels and ticks at 142.5 and 190, the 400C bar (165) sits only 5 units (~10% of a tick gap) below the unticked 170 threshold. A careful student estimating heights can read 400C as ~170 and pick C (or, reading 700C at 163 the same way, D). The key is right on the data but not reliably retrievable from what is drawn.

items.readability_note: Threshold 170 is not a tick; 400C (165) and 700C (163) are within ~5-7 units of it while tick spacing is 47.5. The B/C decision hinges on resolving ~10% of one tick gap by eye. Value labels or a tick/gridline at 170 would fix it; as drawn the key is not reliably readable.
items.note: Data recomputed: 190, 178 >=170; 165, 163 <170. Key correct on data; defect is figure readability.

batch.note: Checked and rejected: (1) Interpolation items P1-Q2, P2-Q3, P3-Q3, P4-Q2, P9-Q3 always key an interior 'between' interval, but each set offers two interior intervals and no mechanical rule (width, upper/lower, centrality) selects the key among them (P1 lower, P2 upper, P3 lower, P4 lower, P9 upper; widths tie or vary), and recognising the stem as an interpolation requires the passage; this is the native ACT format. (2) 'None of the scientists/species' is never the key (P5-Q3, P5-Q5, P6-Q2, P6-Q6, P7-Q2, P7-Q3, P8-Q2) but that only removes one option and never picks the key. (3) 'Agree' item P6-Q4 keys the general option, single item. Topic note: all four RS passages share one template (three experiments, one sharing a control row, interpolation + max + two-condition filter + 'which single change' items), predictable in item TYPE but not in key.
